To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the effects of climate change on the timing of leaf flush and pollen production are modified by the nutrient status of the tree species studied.

(1) the phenological onset date was significantly correlated with foliar concentrations of K, B, Zn, and Ca, which are involved in cell expansion, membrane stability, and photosynthesis and (2) foliar concentrations of Fe were negatively correlated with the amount of pollen, which is in line with the role of Fe in the synthesis of pollen allergens.

(i) higher foliar nutrient concentrations were linked to earlier onset of phenological events, (ii) the amounts of pollen were restricted by higher temperatures, atmospheric NO2 concentrations, and lower foliar iron concentrations, and (iii) urbanization and climate warming interactively influence the timing of plant phenology and the amount of pollen.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new aspect of the complex interplay of climate change, air pollution, and urbanization.
the question of how urbanization affects plant phenology and pollen abundance.
the missing factor of nutrient status in phenological and pollination research.

nutrient status is a missing factor in pollen and phenology research.

phenological and pollen studies should consider the effects of nutrient status.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nutrient status is not only an important factor in the understanding of plant physiology but also in the assessment of climate change impacts.
the nutrient status should be considered as an additional factor in phenological research, and in the future, the nutrient status could also be considered in climate change impact studies.
the effects of air pollution and urbanization on phenology and pollen are not only driven by temperature but that the nutritional status of the trees plays an important role as well.

nutrient availability should be considered in future studies on phenology and pollen, as this might be a missing link between temperature, nutrient status, and phenological onset dates.

the nutrient status of plants is an important factor in the response to climate change and that this factor has been neglected in phenological and allergenic pollen research so far.
